source_excerpts.text:
I have not established the full constant-fraction adversarial quantum fault-tolerance theorem. I cannot supply a uniform compiler satisfying all your conditions, and I have no general impossibility theorem for that compiler statement. The Hamiltonian quantum PCP question remains separately unresolved.

The substantive progress is narrower and precise:

A primary single-shot decoding theorem supplies recovery from adversarial data and syndrome errors, strengthening the available storage operation beyond clean-syndrome decoding.

The new injection paper yields a one-way, outer-code-protected ejection operation with a constant global adversarial radius and explicitly constructible classical control.

Neither operation presently closes into a protected universal computation cycle. I have not constructed the reverse transition, the required logical gates, or an alternative architecture that completes the target.

Below are the constructions, resource accounting, and the exact remaining limitation.

1. Adversarial recovery is available beyond clean syndromes

Gu–Tang–Caha–Choe–He–Kubica’s Single-Shot Decoding of Good Quantum LDPC Codes proves efficient noisy-syndrome decoding for quantum Tanner codes. Its sequential decoder has the following form: for fixed code parameters, there are positive constants  $A_D,B_D,C_D,\beta$  such that

 $A_D|e|_{\mathrm{red}}+B_D|D|
\le C_D n
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|e+\widehat e|_{\mathrm{red}}\le \beta |D|.
\tag{1}$ Here  $e$  is the data error,  $D$  is the syndrome error, and reduced weight means minimum weight modulo stabilizers. The residual bound is independent of the previous data-error weight within the promised domain. The paper also proves stability under repeated rounds. This is credited primary machinery, rather than a new decoding theorem from this attempt. Springer Nature Link [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-04951-6?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

The important feature for the present question is that (1) is a deterministic small-error statement. It does not require independently distributed errors.
